items.name: SIEM
items.rationale: A SIEM is technology that correlates logs and alerts analysts to suspicious activity.

items.name: Log review
items.rationale: People perform the review as an operational process to discover events that already occurred.

items.name: Firewall
items.rationale: A firewall uses technical rules to block disallowed network traffic before it reaches a target.

items.name: IDS
items.rationale: An IDS monitors and alerts on suspicious activity; it does not normally block the traffic.

items.name: IPS
items.rationale: An IPS is placed inline so it can automatically block malicious traffic.

items.name: Encryption
items.rationale: Encryption uses technology to prevent unauthorized readers from understanding protected data.

items.name: MFA
items.rationale: MFA technically enforces multiple factors before granting access, preventing password-only compromise.

items.name: ACL
items.rationale: An ACL is a technical rule set that prevents unauthorized access to a resource or network.

items.name: DLP
items.rationale: DLP can detect sensitive-data movement and, when configured to block it, primarily prevents disclosure.

items.name: FIM
items.rationale: FIM compares files with a known-good baseline and alerts when unauthorized changes are detected.

items.name: Antivirus
items.rationale: Antivirus can block known malware and also detect malware already present; the scenario determines the role.

items.name: Honeypot
items.rationale: A honeypot is decoy technology used to detect and study unauthorized activity.

items.name: Warning banner
items.rationale: A login banner directs users by stating authorized-use rules and can also deter misuse through legal notice.

items.name: System-enforced least privilege
items.rationale: Access-control technology limits accounts to required permissions, preventing excess access.

items.name: Security awareness training
items.rationale: Training is delivered through an operational people process and directs users toward required secure behavior.

items.name: Patch management
items.rationale: The process corrects known software flaws; applying patches also prevents later exploitation.

items.name: Backup restoration
items.rationale: People follow a recovery process to restore data and correct the impact of a failure or attack.

items.name: Incident response
items.rationale: Responders contain, eradicate, and recover from an incident after it occurs.

items.name: Job rotation
items.rationale: Rotating duties can expose irregularities when another person performs and reviews the work.

items.name: Mandatory vacation
items.rationale: Requiring an employee to step away may reveal fraud that depended on continuous concealment.

items.name: Separation of duties
items.rationale: Management divides critical authority so one person cannot complete and conceal a sensitive action alone.

items.name: Background checks
items.rationale: Personnel carry out screening before access is granted to reduce insider risk.

items.name: Penetration test
items.rationale: Authorized testers actively exercise systems to discover exploitable weaknesses.

items.name: Vulnerability scan
items.rationale: Scanning technology detects known weaknesses and reports them for remediation.

items.name: Security policy
items.rationale: Management establishes policy to direct the organization’s required security behavior.

items.name: AUP
items.rationale: An AUP is a management document that tells users what use of organizational systems is permitted.

items.name: Risk assessment
items.rationale: Management evaluates threats, vulnerabilities, likelihood, and impact to identify existing risk.

items.name: NDA
items.rationale: An NDA directs signers not to disclose protected information and helps prevent unauthorized disclosure.

items.name: Change management
items.rationale: Management defines approval and documentation requirements that direct safe changes and prevent unreviewed ones.

items.name: CCTV
items.rationale: Cameras physically monitor an area to detect activity and their visibility may deter intruders.

items.name: Security guards
items.rationale: Guards can block physical entry, notice suspicious activity, and visibly discourage attempts.

items.name: Locks
items.rationale: Locks physically prevent people without the correct key or credential from entering.

items.name: Access control vestibule
items.rationale: The two-door physical space permits one authenticated person at a time and helps prevent tailgating.

items.name: Bollards
items.rationale: Bollards physically stop vehicles from reaching protected areas.

items.name: Fence
items.rationale: A fence visibly discourages entry and can physically delay or prevent access.

items.name: Security lighting
items.rationale: Lighting makes intruders more visible and discourages attempts to approach unnoticed.

items.name: Security signage
items.rationale: A physical sign can discourage entry and direct people by communicating rules or boundaries.

items.name: Fire suppression
items.rationale: Physical suppression systems limit damage and correct the dangerous condition after fire begins.

items.name: Faraday cage
items.rationale: A physical conductive enclosure prevents electromagnetic signals from entering or leaving.

items.name: Manual review used while an automated check is unavailable
items.rationale: A compensating control is an alternate safeguard used when the preferred control cannot be implemented.
